title: Benefit Overpayment Accounts — Earned-Income Deduction in the Waiver Income Count
content:
In the countable annual income on a Benefit Overpayment Accounts waiver request, an earned-income deduction is taken from the annualized earnings for work expenses, by the average hours worked over the certified weeks ending in the income window.

## Schedule

| Average hours worked over the certified weeks ending in the income window | Share of the annualized earnings taken off |
|---|---|
| At least 20 (the full-deduction hours) | 0.05, the full earned-income share (5 percent) |
| Lower than 20 but more than zero | 0.025, the partial earned-income share (2.5 percent) |
| No hours worked | Nothing |

## Terms

- **Certified weeks ending in the income window**: the weekly certifications on the claimant's Unemployment Benefit Claims whose week ending Saturday falls in the three whole months before the handling date (whole months from the week ending date to the handling date fewer than 3).
- **Average hours**: the hours worked reported on those certified weeks, added together and divided by the number of those weeks; with no such week the average is zero.
- **Annualized earnings**: the gross earnings reported on those certified weeks, multiplied by the annualizing multiplier of 4.
- **Deduction**: the annualized earnings multiplied by the share from the schedule, taken off the countable annual income.

## Worked figures (hypothetical)

Six certified weeks end in the window, with 25, 25, 20, 15, 20 and 15 hours worked and USD 900.00 of gross earnings in all. The average is 120 hours divided by 6, which is 20, so the full share applies. The annualized earnings are USD 3,600.00; the deduction is 5 percent of that, USD 180.00. Had the hours averaged 19.5, the deduction would be 2.5 percent, USD 90.00.
